summary.name: FreedomBox
summary.one_liner: FreedomBox is a community project that builds personal servers running free software, with its core web interface and service called FreedomBox Service (Plinth).
use_cases: Replacing a Wi-Fi router with a privacy-focused device
Hosting a personal blog or wiki at home
Operating a Tor relay from home
Hosting a personal website or social network privately
Managing basic system settings like time zone, hostname and automatic upgrades
summary.what_it_does: FreedomBox is a networking appliance meant to run personal servers that use free software for private communications. It hosts applications such as a blog, wiki, website, social network, email, web proxy and Tor relay. FreedomBox Service (Plinth) is its extensible core and web front-end, where each application is a module with a simplified control interface. Plinth can also configure networking, including acting as a wireless router, and basic system settings like time zone, hostname and automatic upgrades. Installation is described as installing Debian (Buster or higher) and running apt install freedombox.
notable: Plinth web interface with modular per-application controls
Can replace a Wi-Fi router as a networking appliance
Installable via apt on Debian (Buster or higher)
caveats: Requires a dedicated machine running Debian (Buster or higher)
Page describes it as a community project, with no commercial support details given
